data.narrative:
GenFab Co, a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Matt Parlmer, has raised $510K to date. The valuation analysis draws on a reference universe of 8 private peers in Robotics & Manufacturing (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics) plus 1 public comparable.

The Peer-Median method was not applicable due to insufficient narrow-filter comparables; only 1 same-stage peer existed in the filtered set, falling short of the 3-datapoint threshold needed for reliable triangulation. Accordingly, analysis relied on Stage-Progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of the Seed-to-next-stage transition. Using GenFab's $510K total raised as a valuation proxy, this method implies a $1.275M valuation.

The analysis supports a range of $1.08M to $1.47M (median $1.28M), centered on the Stage-Progression result. The primary uncertainty is the absence of tight peer comparables at GenFab's stage and tier; while the broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector comprises 9 companies, the lack of multiple same-stage datapoints limits confidence in this single-method estimate. A more robust triangulation would require either additional Seed-stage robotics peers or greater visibility into comparable transaction multiples within the sector.
